decision: two current F5 contract citations point to private Facts; semantic repair requires actual public mathematical Statements, not relabeling them as Postulate
why_postulate_insufficient: Current Postulate explicitly formulates Jordan open/closure equality, but material-transport derivative is only summarized in its private F2; image C1 regularity is only summarized in private F3. The local proof uses derivative in step1.1, image C1 in2.1 and inverse-image graph regularity in3.1.

proposed_body_replacement.old: [F5] [[post-fd-continuum-balances]]: its Fact [F2] gives change of variables and material transport for every compact Jordan set and $C^1$ scalar field under a $C^2$ orientation-preserving motion, componentwise for vector fields; its Fact [F3] gives the open-$C^1$-region/compact-Jordan integral compatibility and the $C^1$ boundary of the diffeomorphic image. Apply these local identities on a relatively compact neighborhood of $\overline V$, translating time so the time under consideration is zero when necessary.
proposed_body_replacement.new: [F5] [[lem-fd-transport-and-density]]: its Statement gives change of variables and material transport for every compact Jordan set and $C^1$ scalar field under the stated $C^2$ orientation-preserving motion, componentwise for vector fields. [[lem-fd-c1-domain-jordan-integrals]]: its Statement gives the open-$C^1$-region/compact-Jordan integral compatibility and the locally $C^1$ graph boundary of the diffeomorphic image. Apply these local identities on a relatively compact neighborhood of $\overline V$, translating time so the time under consideration is zero when necessary.

replace_citations.quote:
For every $t\in I$, change of variables and material transport satisfy

$$\int_{\chi_t(K)}q(t,x)\,dx=\int_Kq(t,\chi(t,a))J(t,a)\,da,$$

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(K)}q(t,x)\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(K)}\bigl(D_tq(t,x)+q(t,x)\theta(t,x)\bigr)\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(K)}\bigl(\partial_tq+\nabla_x\!\cdot(qu)\bigr)\,dx,$$

Then $V$ and $\phi(V)$ are bounded open sets with locally $C^1$ graph boundaries, their compact closures are Jordan measurable, $\partial V$ and $\phi(\partial V)$ have content zero, and

$$\int_{\phi(V)}f(x)\,dx=\int_{\phi(\overline V)}f(x)\,dx.$$

actual_hypothesis_application: For any V compactly contained in B choose bounded open W containing closureV with closureW contained in B. Restrict the original motion to open B as a neighborhood of closureW and translate time t0 to0; supplier transport Statement does not assume chi0=id, so no relabeling of particles is needed. For inverse-image localization, apply C1-region lemma to a small current ball with phi=chi_t^{-1} on Omega_t; compact closure gives V compactly contained in B. Vector momentum transported componentwise.
